title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Sleeve Back. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sleeve Back
options.lineage: Back covers and inner sleeves of independent-label LPs: tracklists, credits, catalogue rhythm
options.thesis: Every Station is the record on the turntable: the Player screen is its sleeve, the history its tracklist.
options.viewport: Player screen: Station art as the sleeve front at commanding scale, the Station name set big and condensed; beside it the day's history as a numbered tracklist, the live row in spot orange with its heart, liner-note credits below; Play in spot orange; Now playing bar along the foot.
options.risk: Tips into a vinyl costume if props (spines, grooves, fake labels) creep in; the type and tracklist rhythm must carry it alone.

raised.raise: Exposure record: every tone snaps to one fixed five-step board ramp; no ad-hoc greys anywhere.
Monochrome product canon: spot orange appears only where audio is live (the playing row, Play, the bar's live mark).
Vertical feed: one Station owns the Player screen; the sleeve front is the largest thing in the window.
Terminal wayfinding: the playing Station is signposted in every view, the Grid included, so you always know where the music is.
Centre rail: text holds a set measure and the margin absorbs window width, so a narrow corner window reads like a wide one.

options.label: Program Guide
options.lineage: Community and college radio program guides: risograph listings zines
options.thesis: SomaFM as this season's listings: every Station a block in the guide, scannable at a glance.
options.viewport: Grid as a listings page: Stations grouped under genre heads in a guide's column rhythm, small art beside each name, the playing Station marked in riso pink; Player screen opens as that Station's guide entry.
options.risk: The familiar radio-app lane (list-of-stations tuners); density can demote artwork and feel like a spreadsheet.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.lineage: Hand-lettered mixtape inlays, side A / side B
options.thesis: Your Liked tracks as the tape you're making from the radio, one side per day.
options.viewport: Player screen with history as a ruled inlay, times right-aligned; Liked view as sides A/B per day. Pinned dark-only: the inlay is translated to dark tape-shell stock with ballpoint-blue ink.
options.case: Listeners love mixtapes (holds audience identification); hand lettering and folds cost glanceability in a corner window.
options.risk: Handwriting at small sizes is unreadable at a glance, which breaks Stay out of the way.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Stations as hatched zones on overlapping sheets.
options.viewport: Overlapping translucent sheets carrying Station zones.
options.case: Listeners do not identify with darkroom notation; hatching obscures playback state.
options.kept: A single fixed tonal ramp as the only tonal tokens.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: A neutral scale with one accent, every claim proven.
options.case: A marketing form, and a grey screen with one accent is the category default; nothing a listener recognises.
options.risk: Generic: the look the redesign is escaping.
options.kept: Accent scarcity: the one live colour is used only a handful of times per screen.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One Station fills the window; the next is a flick away.
options.viewport: Station art edge to edge, glyph rail on the right.
options.case: Scanning ~40 Stations one at a time fails Grid browsing; the feed idiom reads as social video.
options.kept: One subject owns the Player screen at full scale.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Stations as gates, signposted band by band.
options.viewport: Overhead yellow bands with monumental gate numbers.
options.case: Clear wayfinding, but a radio player dressed as an airport confuses more than it guides.
options.kept: The followed destination (the playing Station) stays signposted in every view.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Twinned text columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two small columns held inside a wide margin.
options.case: A reading form on bone paper; neither the audience nor a glance-first player fits it.
options.kept: A set reading measure; the margin absorbs width.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A desktop music player as the big streaming apps ship it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Side nav, art-led Grid, Player with big art and transport, persistent bottom bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other player by design, close to today's look.
